newsitem.title: UK: U.S. stocks mixed in London, Dow seen firm.
newsitem.headline: U.S. stocks mixed in London, Dow seen firm.

text.p: U.S. stocks were mixed in quiet London trading on Wednesday, awaiting any statement from the second day of the Federal Reserve's monetary meeting and braced for Thursday's key jobs report, dealers said.
Treasury bonds were firm in recent London trade, though dealers said there was little activity ahead of an announcement from the Fed's Open Market Committee (FOMC) expected at 1815 GMT.
"All eyes are on the FOMC," said one equity trader in London. "So far there is not even any activity in tobaccos, which is normally a dead certainty."
Dealers said the Dow looked set for a steady-to-firm opening, though the market's performance could depend on May factory goods orders due to be released at 1400 GMT.
Economists were looking for a drop of 0.2 percent on the previous month.
With the Dow having risen 10 quarters in succession, dealers here remained sceptical about its valuation but said a continued flow of good economic data could push the market yet higher.
"You can create a rationale for the market holding firm at these levels, but really it's a question of sentiment and the weight of money," said one.
In the first half of 1997 the Dow rose some 1,200 points.
Stocks expected to be active included McDonald's Corp, which was quoted down $1/4 at $48-3/8 after analysts said the burger maker had suffered an eight-percent decline in June same-store sales.

In contrast, Coca-Cola Co was up $1/8 at $68-3/4 after the company on Tuesday issued a buoyant trading statement, saying it expected worldwide volumes to increase between seven and eight percent, led by buoyant sales in Latin America.
Dealers said Nike Inc could come under pressure after its results after the market close showed slowing sales growth, while Intel Corp could rebound after Tuesday's $2-1/2 tumble.
The benchmark 30-year U.S. Treasury bond was up 3/16 at 98-11/16, to yield 6.73 percent. The June futures contract on the S&P 500 index was up 10.70 points at 931.05.
On Tuesday the Dow closed 49.54 points higher at 7,722.33.
